question: What is the 'Peter principle' argument Catholics use from Matthew 16:18 for the Petrine primacy?

choices.A: Jesus changes Simon's name to 'Rock' (Petros/Kepha) and says on 'this rock' he will build his Church, giving Peter a unique foundational role
choices.B: Peter was the most educated of the apostles and therefore naturally became their leader
choices.C: Jesus selected Peter by lot from among the twelve as an impartial process
choices.D: Peter was the only apostle who never doubted, making him the obvious choice

teaching.title: Peter as Rock — Matthew 16:18
teaching.body: In Matthew 16:18, Jesus says 'You are Peter (Petros/Kepha), and on this rock (petra/kepha) I will build my church.' In the Aramaic (which Jesus spoke), kepha means rock in both uses — there is no gender distinction. The wordplay is a naming act: Simon becomes the Rock upon which the Church is built. Catholics argue this gives Peter a unique authoritative role continued in his successors, the Bishops of Rome. The early Fathers (Cyprian, Origen, Ambrose) widely read Peter as the foundation here.
